subject: ACME MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmark criteria, latency/cost targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmark criteria, latency/cost targets)

Hi Elena —

Great conversation this morning; thanks for the time. Per our call, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (ACME_MAP_v0.2.docx) with the MAP milestone for the technical evaluation. I pulled the technical milestone into the attached technical_eval_template.xlsx so we can be explicit on success criteria, owners, dates, and dependencies.

High level (technical eval milestone):
- Success criteria: model accuracy on ACME intent dataset >= 92% (micro-F1) and hallucination rate < 3% on the 2k blind set.
- Latency targets: P50 <= 180ms for 1-2 concurrent users; P95 <= 350ms under 10 RPS.
- Cost target: tokenized inferencing cost <= $0.0009 per output token at steady-state.
- Model shortlist: LlamaX-13B-quant, Falcon-40B-instruct, MPT-30B-optimized, OpenLlama-2-13B (quantized variants to be evaluated).
- Benchmarks to run: functional accuracy, latency (P50/P95), throughput at 10/50/100 RPS, memory/kv-cache behavior, cost per 1M tokens simulation.

Proposed timeline and owners (draft):
- 2026-03-08: Redwood to provision test endpoints & seed eval dataset (Owner: Marissa/Camila).
- 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12: ACME to run smoke tests + Redwood to run controlled throughput/latency runs (Owner: Michael Grant / ACME technical lead).
- 2026-03-15: Results review and recommended model & config (Owner: Marissa + ACME).
- Target close: 2026-04-01 (commercial review + procurement).

Dependencies: ACME to share sanitized sample dataset and an allowlist for PII; procurement timelines (we flagged 2–3 week SOW review).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm that the latency/cost targets are reasonable for your SLOs.
2) Add any other performance success criteria you care about into the attached sheet.
3) If this looks good, can we schedule a 60-min tech spike on Wed 3/10 where Michael (or your lead architect) and our infra team run the initial runs?

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v0.2.docx, technical_eval_template.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmark criteria, latency/cost targets)

Marissa —

Thanks — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick notes from my side:
- Can we add Diego Morales (our lead ML architect) to the thread? He'll own the dataset prep and run the initial evals. Diego is diego.morales@acme.com.
- For latency/cost: we'd prefer a P50 target closer to 150–200ms (our interactive UX needs ~200ms p50). The cost target of $0.0009/token is in the ballpark — we should quantify tokens per response (avg ~120 tokens) so we can translate to $/query.
- Procurement: I'll loop procurement early but expect a 2–3 week review once we finalize the MAP.

We can do the tech spike on 3/10 — Diego and I are available in the morning PT.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Head of Search & Assistant Products | ACME Corporation
elena.ramos@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@acme.com>, Diego Morales <diego.morales@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmark criteria, latency/cost targets)

Elena / Diego —

Welcome, Diego — thanks for jumping in. I've updated the MAP draft and the technical_eval_template to call out the tokens-per-response estimate and a sample cost calc: at 120 tokens/response and $0.0009/token -> ~$0.108 per query. We'll include a cost projection table in the shared Drive link.

Updated proposed targets (based on Elena feedback):
- Latency: P50 <= 200ms; P95 <= 400ms under 10 RPS. We will also capture P99 tail metrics during the spike.
- Cost: <= $0.0009 per output token (steady-state estimate; will report simulated $/query).

Model shortlist (final draft for the spike):
- LlamaX-13B-quant (fast, quantized)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (higher quality on instruction tasks)
- MPT-30B-optimized (throughput-focused)
- OpenLlama-2-13B (baseline open model)

Spike plan for 2026-03-10 (Redwood infra + ACME Diego/Michael):
- Morning 09:00–11:00 PT: smoke & latency runs (1–10 RPS), P50/P95/P99 capture, token-cost simulation.
- Afternoon 13:00–17:00 PT: throughput runs at 10/50/100 RPS and memory/KV-cache profiling.

Owners:
- Test endpoints & config: Michael Grant (Redwood)
- Dataset prep & privacy review: Diego Morales (ACME)
- Results aggregation & analysis: Camila Reyes + Marissa Cole

Can you confirm Diego's preferred morning window and whether ACME will share a ~2k-row anonymized sample by 3/08? Once confirmed we'll send calendar invites and the Drive folder link.

Marissa

- We can provision endpoints and test harness by 3/08. I'll spin up quantized variants for LlamaX-13B and OpenLlama-2-13B and prepare Falcon-40B and MPT-30B runner configs.
- Suggest we capture both cold-start and warm (KV cache populated) latency; p95 tail is important for UX.
- For cost sim, I'll include tokenization assumptions and a 1M-token simulation to surface $/M tokens and $/query.

I can own the morning slot on 3/10 (09:00–11:00 PT).
